result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give a concrete size order, sensible advice on Devanagari size and line height, tabular figures and print and phone tests. B wins because it warns that a Latin-only font will cause unmatched fallback glyphs for Hindi and tells the reader to check the PDF's font list for embedding and substitution. A covers neither point directly, though it offers a stronger phone-specific layout and the useful advice to match stop-sign spellings. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A covers more of the rubric. It says plainly that a Latin-only font will cause an unmatched fallback for Hindi, and its final checks include confirming in the PDF's font list that both fonts are embedded. B gives stronger phone-layout advice and clearer numeral guidance, but it never warns about Latin-only fonts, and it ranks times above stop names.
